acceptance_criteria.criterion: LoadBitmapAsync disposes the previous Bitmap before replacing.
Dispose() releases the Bitmap without throwing.
dotnet build -c Release reports zero warnings.

summary: Created ThumbnailItemViewModel : ObservableObject, IDisposable with ThumbnailId (long), PositionMs (long), FilePath (string) constructor-set properties.
LoadBitmapAsync: reads bytes async, creates new Bitmap from MemoryStream, disposes old before assigning new.
Dispose(): disposes Bitmap and nulls reference.

comments.note: LoadBitmapAsync disposes old before assigning new (old?.Dispose(); Bitmap = newBitmap) which creates a brief frame where Bitmap is null. Alternative ordering (Bitmap = new; old?.Dispose()) avoids the null frame but risks accessing a disposed object if bound controls retain a reference. Current order matches the spec's stated semantics.

MemoryStream created in LoadBitmapAsync is not explicitly disposed. Bitmap constructor (from stream) reads the stream and typically retains its own internal buffer, so the MemoryStream can be left for GC. This is acceptable but could be wrapped in a using if future profiling shows memory pressure.

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and correct. PositionLabel truncates sub-second precision (format hh:mm:ss), which is the expected behaviour for a UI display label. LoadBitmapAsync correctly captures old reference before nulling it via dispose. Dispose() is null-safe.

LoadBitmapAsync does not check ct before constructing the new Bitmap (only after ReadAllBytesAsync). If cancellation fires between the read and the dispose, the new Bitmap is created and then discarded. This is a very minor resource leak for a single cancelled load, but acceptable.

summary: Code review complete — PASS with one Fix-Forward applied.
PositionLabel uses correct TimeSpan custom format @"hh\:mm\:ss" with escaped colons.
LoadBitmapAsync: reads async with CancellationToken, checks cancellation before Bitmap construction, correct dispose-before-replace ordering.
Fix-Forward: MemoryStream wrapped in 'using' so it is disposed after Bitmap construction. Safe because Bitmap reads the stream fully during construction. Non-behavioral.
Dispose(): null-safe (?.Dispose()), sets Bitmap = null, no GC.SuppressFinalize needed (sealed, no finalizer).

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied: MemoryStream in LoadBitmapAsync wrapped in 'using var ms = new MemoryStream(bytes)' so the stream is disposed after Bitmap construction completes. Bitmap reads the stream fully during construction and does not retain it, so disposal is safe. Non-behavioral change; 643/643 tests pass.
PositionLabel format @"hh\:mm\:ss" correctly escapes the colons for the TimeSpan custom format. AC1 (90500 ms = 00:01:30) verified by manual calculation.

LoadBitmapAsync dispose ordering (capture old = Bitmap, old?.Dispose(), Bitmap = newBitmap) is correct per spec semantics. Brief null window between dispose and assignment is acceptable for a ViewModel load path.
IDisposable implemented without GC.SuppressFinalize(this) — correct since the class is sealed and has no finalizer. No finalizer suppression needed.
